acceptanceCriteria: Spec requirements in the Playwright provider / test-validity spec covering external-origin listing, blocking-vs-incidental classification, the validity finding, pass/fail correlation, the allow-list, and UNKNOWN when network evidence is absent

Fixture-driven tests: a CDN module dependency yields the finding with origin, resource type and first test; an allow-listed origin does not; beacon-only traffic is incidental; a pass/fail pair at one revision names the differing external request
Receipt or report output shows the external-origin list, and the build log records non-goals and limits
body: GitHub issue #1106. A browser test's outcome can depend on resources outside the test environment (an import-map module from a public CDN, analytics or survey scripts, third-party APIs). Observed: 3 of 6 runs at nearly the same revision failed in bulk; the CDN module returned 200, issued no follow-up requests and rendered nothing. The receipt gave no sign of the external dependence. Requested: (1) from run traces or network logs, list requests to origins outside the declared test environment (the app under test plus declared mocks) and classify each as blocking (script/module/awaited XHR or fetch) or incidental (beacons); (2) a validity finding when assertions depend on a page whose blocking resources came from an undeclared external origin, naming the origin, the resource type and the first affected test; (3) correlation of pass/fail splits at the same revision with the external requests that differed between runs (status, timing, missing follow-ups); (4) a project allow-list of external origins accepted as deterministic. Missing network evidence must produce UNKNOWN, never a clean verdict. Related: V1-1737 (#1099, PR #1101), which touches the same jstestprovider request-outcome code.
title: Test validity: report run dependence on undeclared external origins (live CDN modules, third-party scripts) (#1106)
